qc_15_c_l_bration.blurb: This is sector 15 at Lac Long, in the Portneuf region of Quebec, and it holds ten routes, nine of them trad and one sport. The grades start around 5.9 and run up to the low 5.13s, with the bulk in the 5.10 range and a handful of harder lines above 5.11. The wall faces the sun and is known for a few outstanding crack lines, so bring a full trad rack. It sits at the far right end of the lake-side cliff, past the tyrolean crossing, which puts it away from the easier sectors and makes it a spot for experienced leaders rather than beginners.

qc_paroi_des_3_lacs.blurb: A compact beginner-oriented wall in the municipality of Preissac, in Abitibi-Temiscamingue, about ten metres tall with ten routes: seven trad and three sport. Grades are easy to moderate, from around 5.4 to 5.9, so it suits newer climbers learning to place gear or practising on top rope. The rock is granite studded with quartz knobs and cut by horizontal cracks, and the base is level and cleared. The face catches sun through the morning into mid-afternoon. The top is simple to reach for building anchors, and the trail in is short and easy.
